overall: The AG found the School Committee violated the OML by omitting nonunion personnel from its April 9 executive session notice and by not recording a roll call vote in the April 9 minutes; other claims were rejected and the violations were found not intentional.

allegations.summary: April 9 notice allegedly omitted the nonunion personnel to be discussed in executive session (contract negotiations).
allegations.key_passage: We find that the April 9 meeting notice was not sufficiently detailed because the notice failed to identify the non-union personnel with whom the Committee was negotiating under Purpose 2.

allegations.summary: April 9 notice allegedly failed to name the individual against whom the open meeting law complaints were filed.
allegations.key_passage: Because the Open Meeting Law requires a public body to meet to review complaints filed with it, it was sufficiently clear that the complaints being reviewed under Purpose 1 were made against the Committee itself.

allegations.summary: April 9 minutes allegedly failed to record each member's roll call vote when the committee entered executive session.
allegations.key_passage: Even unanimous votes need to be recorded by roll call in the minutes.

allegations.summary: April 23 notice allegedly lacked detail by not identifying the individual against whom complaints were filed and the nonunion personnel to be discussed.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the April 23 meeting notice was sufficiently detailed because the notice identified the non-union personnel, the Interim Superintendent, with whom the Committee was negotiating under Purpose 2, and identified the litigation matter by case name and docket number that the Committee planned to discuss under Purpose 3.

allegations.summary: Complainant urged that the April 9 violations were intentional; the AG considered whether the violations were knowing or intentional.
allegations.key_passage: Because we find no evidence that the Committee acted with deliberate ignorance of the law and where the Committee had not been notified of its obligations prior to the events addressed in this letter, we find that these violations were not intentional.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
remedy_passage: We order the Committee’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and we caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
